page.layout: One printed page. Running head "EMBLEMA" at top centre above the title; page number 77 at top left. Title block in large italic capitals with a continuation line below, full width. Below it a framed engraving (emblem picture) with no text inside. Below the picture, a centred verse of four italic lines. At lower right, a catchword-like word "Vides" set apart in the margin area.

main_text.head: IMPIA FEX HOMINVM REgum mercatur honores.
main_text.p: [Engraving: a crowned king pointing, with two fur-cloaked courtiers in conversation, one holding a bag; no text in the picture.]
main_text.l: Regis in aspectu didici seruire, fauorem
Omne malum Domino clam mens aliena precatur,
Dum facit officium lingua manusq; suum.

page.notes: The title is split across two lines by a hyphen ("RE-" / "gum"); the second line is set in italic and reads "gum mercatur honores." The verse is printed in italic with long s written as f in "fauorem" and "aspectu" as printed. The word "Vides" at lower right is a printed direction word, not a catchword of the running text; it is recorded here as printed. The engraving has no printed text other than the picture itself. Possible ink stains and show-through are not transcribed.
